blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Coaching is not about giving advice. It is about helping someone to think for themselves and find their own answer. A good coach asks good questions, listens carefully, and sits in silence when silence is useful.

Feedback is different — feedback is information, shared with kindness and clarity. A simple model is SBI: Situation, Behaviour, Impact. "In yesterday's meeting, when you interrupted the client three times, the impact was that she stopped sharing her concerns."

Done together, coaching and feedback create a culture where people are not afraid to grow. They stop hiding mistakes and start asking for help — and that is when real development begins.

items.q: According to the text, what is coaching mainly about?
items.why: "It is about helping someone to think for themselves and find their own answer."

items.q: What are the three parts of the SBI model?
items.why: "A simple model is SBI: Situation, Behaviour, Impact."

items.q: In the SBI example, what was the impact of interrupting the client?
options: She asked for a written report
items.why: "the impact was that she stopped sharing her concerns."

items.q: The text suggests that a healthy culture is one where people…
options: feel safe enough to ask for help
rely only on their manager's advice
hide mistakes to protect the team
items.why: Inferência: "They stop hiding mistakes and start asking for help — and that is when real development begins."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The best coaching means telling people exactly what to do.
A coach who stays silent can still be effective.
Growth is easier when people are not afraid to fail.
Feedback works better when it is specific and kind.
items.why: Inferência: o texto abre dizendo que coaching NÃO é dar conselho — dizer exatamente o que fazer contraria a tese.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily conduzindo uma sessão de coaching. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, thanks for making the time. Before we start, this is your conversation, not mine — I'm just here to help you think out loud. You said you're drowning in work at the moment. Tell me a bit more about that.

Right. So the team is capable, but the tasks keep landing back on your desk. Can I check I've understood? You feel that if you hand something over, it won't be done to your standard, so you take it back. Is that fair?

Okay. Let me ask you something. When you were a team member yourself, did your old manager delegate everything perfectly? No — so people learned by doing it imperfectly at first. What would change if you saw a few mistakes as data rather than as failure?

I can see that landed. Here's what I'd offer you: pick one task this week that only you are doing right now, and give it away completely. Don't rescue it. We'll talk next Friday about what happened. Does that feel like a fair first step?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Emily describe her role at the start of the session?
options: She is there to review his performance
She is there to give the best advice
She is there to set his weekly targets
She is there to help him think out loud
items.why: "this is your conversation, not mine — I'm just here to help you think out loud."

items.q: What problem does the team leader describe?
options: He has too few people on the team
Tasks keep landing back on his desk
His team is not capable enough
His manager gives him unclear goals
items.why: "the tasks keep landing back on your desk."

items.q: When Emily says "Can I check I've understood?", what is she doing?
items.why: Inferência: ela reformula com as próprias palavras o que ele disse para confirmar — escuta ativa / paraphrasing.

items.q: Why does Emily mention his own old manager?
options: To help him see that people learn by doing imperfectly
To prove that delegation always fails
To criticise the way he was trained
To suggest he find a new mentor
items.why: Inferência: ela reenquadra o medo de erros mostrando que ninguém delega perfeitamente e que se aprende fazendo.

items.q: What concrete step does Emily agree with him?
options: To hire an assistant this week
To write a report on his workload
To give one task away completely and not rescue it
items.why: "pick one task this week… give it away completely. Don't rescue it."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She practised active listening, nodding and reflecting back what she heard." Active listening is…
options: fully focusing on the speaker and showing you understand
waiting quietly for your turn to speak
asking many quick questions in a row
taking detailed notes during a meeting
items.why: Active listening = escuta ativa: concentrar-se no outro e demonstrar que entendeu.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Without ___, people won't admit mistakes, so honest feedback becomes impossible."
items.why: Psychological safety = segurança psicológica: sem ela, ninguém assume erros.

items.q: "Everyone has a blind spot — something obvious to others but invisible to us." A blind spot is…
options: a strength you rely on too much
a weakness you already understand well
a habit or flaw you cannot see in yourself
a goal you have not set yet
items.why: Blind spot = ponto cego: aquilo que você não enxerga em si mesmo.

items.q: Choose the correct verb: "A good coach will ___ the problem, helping you see it as a chance to learn instead of a failure."
items.why: To reframe = reenquadrar: transformar um problema em oportunidade de aprendizado.

items.q: "He asked an open question to get her thinking." An open question is one that…
options: is only used at the end of a meeting
can be answered with yes or no
items.why: Open question = pergunta aberta: não se responde com sim/não; abre espaço para reflexão.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas de coaching e feedback. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's touch base next Friday to see how the task went." To touch base means to…
items.why: Touch base = dar um alô, ter um contato rápido para se atualizar.

items.q: "I'd like to follow up on the feedback I gave you last week." To follow up on means to…
options: revisit it and check on progress
items.why: Follow up on = retomar algo e verificar o andamento.

items.q: "When you delegate, don't step in the moment something goes wrong." To step in means to…
items.why: Step in = intervir, entrar na jogada para assumir o controle.

items.q: "Try not to sugarcoat the feedback — be kind, but be clear." To sugarcoat means to…
options: make something sound better than it is
items.why: Sugarcoat = dourar a pílula, suavizar demais para esconder o problema.

items.q: "Give the task away completely and let them figure it out." To figure something out means to…
options: ask you to do it instead
work it out and find the solution
items.why: Figure it out = descobrir sozinho como resolver.
